frequency_question: How often does institutional and bureaucratic friction successfully prevent or indefinitely stall proposed countercyclical capital buffer adjustments or equivalent macroprudential rule changes once initiated?
membership_rule: Includes all formal proposals, working papers, or inter-agency discussions regarding the activation or calibration of the CCyB or equivalent systemic risk capital surcharges by the Federal Reserve Board since the establishment of the framework post-2010.

cases.name: Post-Pandemic Holistic Capital Review / Basel III Endgame Inter-agency Friction Delay

coverage_note: 4 major formal review periods identified where the CCyB level was explicitly on the table for active adjustment.
known_gaps: Informal deliberations and unpublicized staff debates on capital buffers are not fully captured in public dockets.
skeleton: Total formal formal review cycles of the countercyclical capital buffer where activation was actively contemplated by staff or governors, categorized by whether structural friction/inter-agency pushback successfully held the rate at 0% vs resulting in an increase.
multiplier: 2 increases or substantive structural adjustments considered vs 2 stalls/holds at 0% due to friction and banking sector pushback over the historical lifetime of the instrument.
validity_reason: The regulatory framework and institutional inertia governing bank capital requirements evolve slowly across congressional and administrative cycles.
